name: create()
syntax:
import { create } from 'zustand'
const useStore = create((set, get) => ({ ... }))
description: Creates a Zustand store and returns a React hook used to read and subscribe to that store from any component.
parameters: stateCreatorFn — a function receiving (set, get, api) that returns the initial state object plus any actions.
returns: A hook function (e.g. useStore) that components call to access the store's state and actions.
notes: create() lives outside React component code — typically in its own module — and the returned hook is imported wherever the store is needed.

name: Defining a store
description: A Zustand store is a single object combining both state values and the actions that update them, defined once via create() and shared across the app.
notes: Unlike Redux, there's no separate reducer/action-type boilerplate — state and the logic that changes it live together in one function.

name: Store as a hook
description: The value returned by create() is a standard React hook, so any component can call it directly to subscribe to store updates without wrapping it in a Provider.
returns: The selected piece of state (or the whole state object if no selector is passed).
notes: Calling the hook with no selector, e.g. useBearStore(), returns the entire state object and re-renders on any change.

name: No Provider needed
description: Zustand stores are plain modules, not React context — there is no <Provider> to wrap the app in, and any component can import the hook and use it directly.
example:
// No <StoreProvider> wrapping required — just import and call the hook
import { useBearStore } from './store';
notes: This is a key differentiator from Redux (react-redux's <Provider>) and React Context, which both require wrapping the component tree.

name: Multiple stores
description: Zustand encourages splitting state into several small, independent stores (e.g. useUserStore, useCartStore) rather than one large global store.
example:
const useUserStore = create((set) => ({ user: null }));
const useCartStore = create((set) => ({ items: [] }));
notes: Multiple stores keep concerns isolated and avoid unrelated components re-rendering from unrelated state changes.

name: Store outside React
description: Every store created by create() exposes getState() and setState() directly on the hook, allowing state to be read or updated from outside React components (e.g. utility functions, event listeners).
returns: getState() returns the current state object; setState() applies a partial update.
notes: Useful for non-React code such as API clients or analytics that need to read or update store state.
